gaps.sentence: The company ___ its first quarterly profit in a decade last spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Last spring' is a finished time reference, so the past simple is required.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were in hospital — why did nobody tell me?
gaps.explanation: The finding out is in the past, so the past simple 'didn't know' is used.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the doctor's on Tuesday; I made the appointment yesterday.
gaps.hint: a fixed appointment arranged for the future
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am going.
